title: vSphere Distributed Port Blocked or Disconnected
exclusions: Returns complete native `DvsPortBlockedEvent` and `DvsPortDisconnectedEvent` records at vCenter event-key grain. Broadcom defines the first as a port blocked in a distributed virtual switch and the second as a port disconnected; the event does not by itself prove packet loss, an outage, VLAN/MTU mismatch, uplink failure, malicious action, current port state or root cause. The former can provide status detail, runtime information and previous block state; the latter can provide port key and connectee, but optional properties may be absent. The rule intentionally excludes nonexistent `VmnicDisconnectedEvent` and does not represent VDS health-check results, physical NIC state, ordinary VM disconnect events, distributed-switch configuration drift, or performance counters. Every complete qualifying event is returned without a count threshold. It changes no port or switch.
evidence: After deployment, retain vCenter/DVS/dvPort/connectee/VM/host/uplink inventory; add-on event-task and DCN revisions; representative raw blocked/disconnected events with eventClass, key, createdTime, dvs.name/reference, portKey, connectee or runtime/status fields, userName, message, vCenter, event/index times; independent pipeline and current-port/topology health; maintenance/change records; version-controlled `vcenter_dvs_port_connectivity_events` SPL, ACL, schedule, dispatches and rows; runbook/dashboard and disposition; and dated blocked, disconnected, wrong-class, optional-field, duplicate, delayed, migration and current-state tests. This editorial review generated no DVS event, port change, Splunk execution, alert, incident or production validation evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In one closed isolated bucket, ingest a complete `vim.event.DvsPortBlockedEvent` with DVS `Prod-VDS`, portKey `101`, statusDetail, previous state and unique key, plus a complete `vim.event.DvsPortDisconnectedEvent` for portKey `102` and a connectee with another key. Expect exactly two rows labeled `blocked` and `disconnected`, preserving vCenter/DVS/port/event identity and UC-2.1.19.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero rows for `VmDisconnectedEvent`, HostDisconnectedEvent, arbitrary event names/wildcards, wrong source/index/sourcetype, blank vCenter/key/DVS/portKey/action, outside-bucket data and exact replay. Separate health must expose missing event collection, optional schema drift, stale topology and disagreement with current DVPort state.

dataSources: Primary source is vCenter Events API data collected by Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics with pool task `event` into the deployment-selected event index (documented default `index=vmware-taskevent`) and `sourcetype=vmware_inframon:events`. Required native properties are exact `eventClass`, unique `key`, `createdTime`, `dvs.name`, `portKey`, vCenter/host and event/index time; `statusDetail`, `runtimeInfo`, `prevBlockState`, `connectee`, `userName` and `fullFormattedMessage` are event-specific context. Current DVS/DVPort/uplink topology, VDS health checks, performance counters, maintenance and change records corroborate.
app: Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics (Splunkbase 5089) collects vCenter event objects through DCNs. A local network-operations app owns source/current-state health, topology/change enrichment, saved search, dashboard, tests, routing and runbook.
spl:
index=vmware-taskevent sourcetype="vmware_inframon:events" (eventClass="vim.event.DvsPortBlockedEvent" OR eventClass="vim.event.DvsPortDisconnectedEvent") earliest=-15m@m latest=-10m@m
| spath path=dvs.name output=dvs_name
| spath path=connectee.connectedEntity.value output=connectee_moid
| eval vcenter=lower(coalesce(nullif(trim(vcenter),""),nullif(trim(host),""))), event_key=trim(tostring(key)), port_key=trim(tostring(portKey)), actor=coalesce(nullif(trim(userName),""),"unknown"), port_event=case(eventClass="vim.event.DvsPortBlockedEvent","blocked",eventClass="vim.event.DvsPortDisconnectedEvent","disconnected")
| where len(vcenter)>0 AND len(event_key)>0 AND len(dvs_name)>0 AND len(port_key)>0 AND len(port_event)>0
| eval event_identity=vcenter."|".event_key
| dedup event_identity
| eval use_case="UC-2.1.19", event_time=strftime(_time,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
| table _time vcenter event_key port_event dvs_name port_key connectee_moid actor statusDetail prevBlockState fullFormattedMessage event_time _indextime use_case
| sort 0 -_time vcenter event_key
description: Surfaces each complete vCenter event recording that a distributed-switch port became blocked or disconnected during a closed five-minute bucket. Results preserve DVS, port, event and available connectee/status context without inferring network impact or cause.
value: Exact native event monitoring gives virtualization and network teams an early, searchable record of distributed-port connectivity changes. Avoiding wildcard and invented event classes reduces false investigations and directs responders to current topology, policy, uplink and performance evidence.
implementation: Enable vCenter event collection, prove the two event schemas and source health, and schedule the fixed delayed search every five minutes. Reconcile each row with current DVPort/VDS/connectee/uplink state, maintenance and related changes/metrics before escalation; never unblock or reconnect a port automatically.
visualization: Use an event table with time, vCenter, event class/action, DVS, port key, connectee, status detail, previous block state, actor, current DVPort state, topology, maintenance, owner and disposition. Add trends by DVS/port/action plus separate event-pipeline and stale-topology panels. Do not label the table `uplink failures` or `packet loss`.
schema: Native vSphere DvsPortBlockedEvent and DvsPortDisconnectedEvent objects
dataModelAcceleration: No CIM dataset documents vSphere DVS event subclasses, port keys, connectees or block-state details. Raw event identity remains authoritative.

Splunkbase: Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics

knownFalsePositives:
The event is genuine, but the condition may be expected or transient.

1. **Approved VM/vNIC reconfiguration** — disconnect/reconnect workflows can produce port events. Match exact VM/connectee, change and interval.

2. **vMotion or host maintenance** — topology transitions may disconnect or recreate port relationships. Correlate migration and maintenance events.

3. **Intentional administrative block** — security, quarantine or decommission policy may block a port. Verify actor, policy, approval, scope and current state.

4. **DVS/port-group maintenance** — switch upgrade or policy deployment can create expected transitions. Check change record and all affected ports.

5. **Transient control-plane state** — a port can recover quickly. Compare current DVPort runtime and subsequent events rather than assuming continuing outage.

6. **Optional-field absence** — connectee or status detail may legitimately be absent for an event subtype/version. Preserve raw event; required DVS/port identity still governs detection.

7. **Collector replay** — duplicate route/checkpoint can repeat event keys. Dedup covers one bucket; health must detect cross-bucket replay.

8. **Port-key/topology reuse or drift** — a port key is interpreted in DVS/vCenter scope and mappings change. Use vCenter+DVS+port and event-time inventory.

**Suppression mechanism:** use a governed post-result lookup keyed by vCenter, DVS identity, port key, exact eventClass and approved interval, with owner, reason and finite expiry. Retain raw events and source/current-state health; never suppress an entire DVS.
mitreAttack: N/A (distributed virtual-switch connectivity event; no adversary behavior asserted)
detectionType: Raw vCenter DVS port blocked/disconnected event
reviewer: Source-backed editorial review; production VMware/network/Splunk SME validation pending

cost.search_load_notes: Bounded event search over two exact event classes; topology reconciliation is separate.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and event scope

Assign vSphere networking, physical network, workload and Splunk owners. Inventory vCenters, DVS identities, port keys, port groups, connectees, ESXi hosts/uplinks, maintenance and owner routing. Broadcom documents exact DvsPortBlockedEvent and DvsPortDisconnectedEvent classes. Do not use a wildcard or nonexistent VmnicDisconnectedEvent as a production contract.

## Step 1 — Collect and prove event objects

Deploy supported Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics, configure read-only vCenter API access over TCP 443 and include `event` in the collection pool. Verify the actual event index, documented default `vmware-taskevent`, and `vmware_inframon:events`.

Compare representative raw JSON with vSphere Client Tasks and Events. Prove `eventClass`, event `key`, `dvs.name`, `portKey`, vCenter/host, `_time` and `_indextime`. For blocked events validate statusDetail/runtimeInfo/prevBlockState when present; for disconnected events validate connectee when present. Preserve `fullFormattedMessage` for operators but do not parse localized text as primary identity.

Build independent health for expected vCenters, event-job success/records_written, ordinary event flow, field completeness, schema/version drift, p99 delay, duplicate keys, API/auth and DCN failures, and current topology freshness.

## Step 2 — Save the closed-bucket search

Save sidecar SPL as `vcenter_dvs_port_connectivity_events`, every five minutes. At 12:15 it searches 12:00–12:05. Shift both time bounds together after delay measurement and reconcile late events separately.

The query filters two exact classes, uses `spath` for structured DVS/connectee properties, requires vCenter/event/DVS/port/action, and deduplicates vCenter+event key. It records unknown actor rather than discarding system events. No count threshold or root-cause mapping is added.

## Step 3 — Validate event and current state

Use fixtures for blocked and disconnected events with and without optional fields; unrelated DVS, VM and host events; blank required fields; duplicate/same key across vCenters; same port key across DVSs; localized message; delayed/future time; replay and wrong source. Assert no uplink/packet-loss claim.

In a nonproduction DVS, perform owner-approved reversible port block/unblock and vNIC disconnect/reconnect tests. Capture vCenter event, current DVPort runtime, connectee, topology and Splunk timing. Do not disrupt production or infer that the event persists after recovery.

## Step 4 — Operationalize and respond

Enrich after detection with current/event-time DVS port, connectee VM/vNIC, host/uplink, port group, VLAN/MTU/team policy, maintenance and change. Triage: verify raw event; inspect current DVPort state and subsequent events; resolve actor/change; map topology; correlate VM/host/network metrics and application SLOs; then identify administrative action, migration, policy, control-plane or path fault.

Never automatically unblock, reconnect, migrate, reconfigure VDS/port group, alter VLAN/MTU/teaming or restart networking. Require VMware/network/workload approval, out-of-band access, rollback and service validation.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot

- No events: verify pool `event`, vCenter credentials/443, scheduler/DCN, event index/RBAC and common-event health.
- DVS or port null: inspect native JSON and subtype; validate `spath` and add-on version, not message regex alone.
- Connectee null: it is optional; use event/current topology and do not drop a valid blocked event.
- Current port healthy: classify recovered/transient after checking subsequent events and impact.
- Many ports affected: inspect shared DVS, host/uplink, policy deployment and control-plane changes.
- Duplicate events: compare vCenter/key, windows, routes and checkpoints.
- Physical uplink suspected: collect physical NIC and external-switch evidence; these two DVPort events do not prove it.

Keep draft status until VMware, network and Splunk owners validate source, fixtures, current-state reconciliation and response. Documentation review is not runtime assurance.
grandmaExplanation: We show when the virtualization manager records that a port on its shared virtual switch was blocked or disconnected. The team then checks whether the change was planned, whether the port recovered, and whether anyone actually lost connectivity.
hardware: vSphere Distributed Switches and distributed virtual ports managed by vCenter; physical NICs and external switches are corroborating layers.
